intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white pebble shore, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street foods like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A feast for all the senses and a true taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the legendary Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its shallow pink-tinged sands and crystal-clear lagoon waters. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small islet, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by local bus or rental car.
experiences.location: Elafonissi Beach, Chania Regional Unit, Crete

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania where a local chef teaches you to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drenched loukoumades. You'll visit a local market beforehand to source fresh ingredients and finish with a communal meal paired with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach, two of Mykonos's most celebrated shores with clear blue waters and golden sand. As the sun sets, head to a waterfront taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner of fresh grilled octopus, saganaki, and local wine while watching the famous Mykonos windmills glow in the twilight.
experiences.location: Paradise Beach & Little Venice, Mykonos Town, Mykonos

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at airport, clear customs, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unpack, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a short walk along the beach to get your bearings and enjoy the sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the local waterfront promenade to explore the nearest village. Browse small shops and get a feel for the local atmosphere. Watch the sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget-friendly gyro or souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or en route to the hotel (€3–5).
meals.dinner: Find a local taverna near the resort serving traditional Greek mezedes. Try tzatziki, olives, and grilled octopus. Budget around €12–15 per person including a small carafe of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash or withdraw euros at the airport ATM for small local vendors. Keep receipts for tracking your budget.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a swim at the beachfront right outside the resort. The sea is warm and calm in the morning. Walk along the shoreline and collect seashells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local market or village square. Pick up fresh fruit, local honey, and olives from market stalls. Visit a small local bakery for traditional koulouri (sesame bread rings) and tiropita (cheese pie).
day_by_day.evening: Head to a beachside bar for a budget-friendly sunset drink. Try a local Mythos or Alfa beer (€2–3). Afterwards, dine at a simple psarotaverna (fish taverna) with fresh catch of the day.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts from a nearby café or supermarket (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Fresh bread, olives, feta, and tomatoes from the local market — assemble your own picnic on the beach (€5–6 total).
meals.dinner: Grilled fish or calamari at a local psarotaverna with a Greek salad and house wine (€14–16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen as temperatures reach 29°C. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic church accessible by local bus or on foot. Explore the ruins and learn about the region's history through free or low-cost entry sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for snorkeling in the clear warm water. Rent basic snorkel gear from a local beach rental shop (€5–8) and explore the underwater rocks and small fish near the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost guided walking tour of the local village if available, or self-guide using a downloaded offline map. Explore narrow whitewashed alleys and blue-domed churches.

meals.breakfast: Toasted bread with local olive oil and tomatoes at the hotel or a nearby café (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and a cold Nescafé frappé from a local bakery (€4–5).
meals.dinner: Traditional moussaka and a Greek salad at a family-run taverna in the village (€11–14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus schedules the evening before to plan your morning archaeological site visit efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a bicycle to visit a quieter, less-touristy beach nearby. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Enjoy swimming and sunbathing in a more secluded setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby fishing village on foot. Watch local fishermen mend nets and bring in their catch. Browse small craft shops for affordable souvenirs like ceramic tiles or olive wood items.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from the local market if your accommodation has kitchen access, or dine at a budget souvlaki joint in the village.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and a Greek coffee from a local kafeneion (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood snack like grilled sardines or fried whitebait from a small harbour-side grill (€6–8).
meals.dinner: Souvlaki platter with pita, tzatziki, and chips at a local grill house (€8–10 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rentals typically cost €8–12 per day and are a great budget-friendly way to explore the coastline.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely morning at the hotel beach. Try paddleboarding or kayaking if the resort or nearby beach rental offers it (€8–12/hour). Enjoy the calm morning sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove or small winery offering free or low-cost tastings. Learn about traditional Greek olive oil production and sample local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor cultural event, local festival, or live Greek music night at a taverna if available in June. Ask hotel staff for local event recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — eggs, olives, feta, bread, and fresh juice (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Dakos (Cretan rusk salad with tomato and feta) and a cold drink at a seaside café (€6–8).
meals.dinner: Lamb kleftiko or slow-cooked goat at a traditional taverna — a hearty and affordable local specialty (€12–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: June often features local saint's day celebrations (panigiri) with free food and music. Ask locals about any upcoming events.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning walk or light hike along a coastal path near the resort. Enjoy panoramic sea views, wildflowers, and fresh air before the heat of the day sets in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beach. Build sandcastles, read a book, or simply relax under the sun. The sea is warm enough for extended swimming sessions.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local night market or artisan fair if available. Pick up affordable handmade jewelry, ceramics, or local spices as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri sesame ring and a Greek coffee from a street vendor (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Homemade-style bean soup (fasolada) and crusty bread at a traditional kafeneion (€5–7).
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled sea bream or sea bass with lemon and herbs at a waterfront taverna (€13–16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The coastal path walk is best done before 9:00 AM to avoid peak heat. Bring water and wear a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip option: Take a local ferry or bus to a nearby island or coastal town for a change of scenery. Research affordable day-trip ferry routes (€10–20 return) from the nearest port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip destination — visit its main beach, central square, and any notable landmarks. Enjoy the different atmosphere and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Relax on the beach and watch the sunset. Reflect on the week's highlights over a quiet drink.

meals.breakfast: Pack a simple breakfast from the supermarket — yogurt cup, banana, and water — to eat on the ferry (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Eat at a local taverna at the day-trip destination. Try whatever the daily special is for the best value (€10–13 per person).
meals.dinner: Light meal back near the resort — a mezedes platter of dips, bread, and olives shared between two (€10–12 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance and book tickets at the port early in the morning to secure a spot on budget routes.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and take a gentle swim. Use the morning to do laundry, reorganize your bag, and plan the second week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local museum or cultural center with low entry fees (€3–6). Learn about the regional history, Byzantine art, or local maritime heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Try a different local neighborhood for dinner. Walk 10–15 minutes from the resort to find a less touristy taverna with more authentic and affordable food.

meals.breakfast: Full relaxed breakfast at the resort or a nearby café with fresh orange juice, eggs, and pastries (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Cheese and tomato toastie or a simple sandwich from a local bakery (€3–5).
meals.dinner: Stuffed vegetables (gemista — tomatoes and peppers stuffed with rice and herbs) at a traditional taverna (€10–13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip is a good time to reassess your budget spending. Review your expenses and adjust the remaining days if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or join a shared minibus tour to explore a stretch of coastline with multiple beaches. Visit 2–3 different beaches in one morning to compare and find your favorite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle at the most beautiful beach you discovered in the morning. Swim, snorkel, and sunbathe for the afternoon. Bring a packed lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out for a leisurely evening walk and stop at a local ice cream shop for a scoop of Greek-style gelato (pagoto).

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with honey and granola from a café near the scooter rental (€4–5).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the supermarket — pita bread, hummus, cucumber, and fruit (€5–6 total).
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken souvlaki skewers with tzatziki and pita at a local grill restaurant (€9–12 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs €15–25 per day. Always wear a helmet and check that your travel insurance covers scooter use.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided tour of the local village. Visit the main church, central plateia (square), and any historic fountains or monuments. Chat with locals at the kafeneion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a free beach yoga or fitness session if offered by the resort or a local instructor. Alternatively, spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing at the hotel beach.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate the trip's midpoint. Choose a well-reviewed local restaurant with fresh seafood and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) and a freddo espresso at a local café (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Light lunch of Greek salad with extra feta and a cold Mythos beer at a beach bar (€8–10).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a seafood dinner — lobster pasta or grilled prawns with local white wine. Budget €20–25 per person for this special meal.

day_by_day.notes: This is a good evening to try the local specialty wine or ouzo as an aperitif before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local farmers' market or weekly street market if available. Stock up on fresh produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and artisan goods at very low prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a creative afternoon at the beach — try building a driftwood sculpture, sketching the coastline, or writing a travel journal. Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple Greek meal using market ingredients if kitchen access is available. Alternatively, enjoy a casual dinner at a local gyros shop.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and fruit bought from the morning farmers' market (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Homemade picnic on the beach with market purchases — bread, olives, feta, tomatoes, and fruit (€5–7 total).
meals.dinner: Gyros pita wrap with fries and a cold drink at a local gyros shop (€6–8 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Farmers' markets typically happen on specific weekdays. Ask hotel staff which day and where the nearest one is held.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip or join a budget group sea excursion to explore sea caves, hidden coves, or nearby uninhabited islets. Many local operators offer affordable half-day trips (€15–25 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat trip and spend the afternoon at the beach. Use the last full beach day to swim, snorkel, and soak up the sun.
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner at your favorite taverna from the trip. Order dishes you haven't tried yet — perhaps pastitsio (Greek lasagna) or kokoretsi if adventurous.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the boat trip — a banana, yogurt, and water from the supermarket (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Eat on the boat or at a small harbour café upon return — simple grilled fish or a sandwich (€7–10).
meals.dinner: Celebratory final dinner at the best local taverna you've discovered during the trip. Budget €15–18 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat excursion the day before to secure a spot, especially in June when tourism picks up.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Greece. Wake up early for a final sunrise swim in the warm Mediterranean sea. Pack your bags and do a final check of the room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort and head to the airport or port for departure. If time allows before checkout, enjoy one last Greek coffee at a seafront café and browse any last-minute souvenir shops.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry snacks and water for the journey home. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, local food, and Greek culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and a strong Greek coffee at a beachside café (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or pack leftovers and market items for the journey (€5–8).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Keep some euros aside for airport coffee or last-minute purchases.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight lands and immigration/baggage claim completed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in. Once settled, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea right at the resort beach — no agenda, just relaxation and orientation.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the nearest waterfront promenade as the sun sets. Explore the local harbor area, watch fishing boats come in, and soak in the Greek atmosphere for the first time.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a casual seaside snack bar near the resort upon arrival — try a classic Greek gyros wrap (around €4–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range taverna near the resort. Order a mezze spread: tzatziki, taramasalata, grilled octopus, and fresh bread. Budget around €20–25 per person with a glass of local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you've just traveled. Hydrate well, apply sunscreen, and rest early to beat jet lag and be fresh for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the resort, head to the nearest local beach early (before 10:00) to claim a good spot. Swim in the warm Aegean, snorkel if equipment is available, and enjoy the calm morning waters before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local village or town center on foot or by local bus. Explore the main square (plateia), browse small shops selling local olive oil, honey, and ceramics. Visit a local bakery (fournos) for fresh koulouri and pastries.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a sunset viewing from a clifftop or elevated point near the resort area. Afterward, enjoy dinner at a family-run taverna in the village.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh orange juice, and a freddo cappuccino (€6–10)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — fresh watermelon, a Greek salad, and sparkling water (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Family taverna in the village — grilled sea bream (tsipoura), village salad, and a carafe of house white wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start wearing sunscreen from early morning. The June sun is strong by 9:00 AM. A hat and reef-safe sunscreen are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip or water taxi to a nearby secluded cove or sea cave — many Greek coastal resorts offer these for €15–25 per person. Swim in crystal-clear turquoise water away from the main beach crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Relax by the pool or beach. In the late afternoon, visit a local fish market or farmers' market if one is operating nearby to see fresh local produce and seafood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or food tasting experience at a local culinary studio — learn to make spanakopita, tzatziki, or fresh pasta. Many mid-range options run €35–50 per person and include dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the boat trip — toast, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the boat trip or eat at a small waterfront café upon return — cheese pie (tyropita), olives, and lemonade (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Included in the cooking class experience, or a casual souvlaki spot if skipping the class (€12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip and cooking class at least one day in advance through the resort concierge or local tour operators.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient archaeological site or Byzantine church within reach of the resort. Explore with a self-guided audio tour or a local guide (€10–15). History and context make the beaches feel even more special.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a long afternoon swim session. Rent a paddleboard or kayak (€10–20/hour) and explore the coastline at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a harbor-side dinner as fishing boats are lit up in the evening. Watch locals gather for their evening volta (stroll) along the seafront.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the archaeological site — bougatsa (custard pastry) and Greek coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Waterfront café — shrimp saganaki, fresh bread, and a cold Mythos beer (€16–20)
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant at the harbor — grilled whole fish priced by the kilo, plus a Greek salad and tzatziki (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the archaeological site. Bring a refillable water bottle — staying hydrated in 29°C heat is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning at the resort beach. Sleep in, swim, and enjoy a slow breakfast. This is a deliberate rest morning to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or rent a scooter/ATV (€25–40/day) to explore a different beach on the same island or coastline — aim for one with a different character, such as a pebbly cove or a windswept sandy stretch.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop bar or terrace restaurant for sundowner cocktails — try an Aperol Spritz or a local mastiha liqueur cocktail. Stay for dinner as the stars come out.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — eggs, fresh fruit, yogurt, and cold-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at the new beach — fried calamari, a cold Greek salad, and freshly squeezed lemonade (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Rooftop terrace restaurant — lamb chops (paidakia), roasted vegetables, and local red wine (€24–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter or ATV, ensure you have a valid license and wear a helmet. Roads can be narrow and winding near coastal areas.

day_by_day.morning: Join an early morning snorkeling or scuba diving excursion (€30–60 per person depending on equipment and guide). Explore underwater rock formations, sea grass beds, and possibly spot octopus, sea urchins, and small fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the excursion, visit a local olive grove or winery for a tasting tour. Many Greek islands have small family-run producers who welcome visitors for €10–20 including tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a nearby traditional neighborhood (chora or old town) after dark when it's cooler. Browse artisan shops and enjoy the whitewashed architecture lit by lanterns.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-excursion breakfast — energy bar, banana, and coffee from the resort
meals.lunch: Post-dive taverna — dakos (Cretan rusk salad), grilled sardines, and a cold Fix beer (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Chora restaurant — moussaka, stuffed tomatoes (gemista), and a glass of local Assyrtiko white wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Do not eat a heavy meal before the diving/snorkeling excursion. The winery visit is best in the late afternoon when temperatures begin to drop slightly.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of the trip — take a half-day guided walking food tour of the local area. Visit the central market, taste cured meats, local cheeses, olives, and honey, and learn about the food culture from a local guide (€25–40 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the resort. Enjoy the pool, read a book, and take a nap. A deliberate slow afternoon to reset for the second half of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the summer solstice sunset (June 21 is the longest day of the year). Find a scenic clifftop or beach-facing terrace. Celebrate with a special dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light — the food tour will include many tastings throughout the morning
meals.lunch: Included in the food tour tastings, supplemented by a light mezze plate at a market café (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Special solstice dinner at the best-reviewed mid-range restaurant in the area — fresh pasta with seafood, a bottle of local wine, and a dessert of loukoumades (honey doughnuts) (€30–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: June 21 is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year. Sunset will be late (around 20:30–21:00), making for a spectacular evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by ferry or boat to a nearby island or coastal town (if applicable to your resort location). Depart early to maximize time. Explore the new destination's main town and waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the day-trip destination's beach, which may have a different character from your home base. Have lunch locally and explore backstreets and churches.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry/boat back to the resort area. Fresher, windswept, and full of new memories. Quiet dinner close to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — keep it light
meals.lunch: Local taverna at the day-trip destination — grilled fish of the day, village salad, and house wine (€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the resort upon return — souvlaki plate or a pita wrap with a cold beer (€12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry/boat schedules in advance and book tickets the day before. Return ferries can fill up in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or stretching session on the beach at sunrise (many beachfront resorts offer this, or simply do your own session on the sand). Follow with a long, unhurried swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local ceramics workshop or artisan studio. Watch craftspeople at work and try your hand at painting a small piece to take home as a souvenir (€15–25 including materials).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live Greek music performance — look for a taverna hosting live bouzouki or laïká music. This is a quintessential Greek cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast — smoothie bowl, granola, and Greek yogurt with fresh figs
meals.lunch: Artisan quarter café — mezze plate, hummus, and pita with fresh lemonade (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Taverna with live music — shared mezze feast: dolmades, fava, grilled halloumi, and slow-roasted lamb (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Live music tavernas often don't get going until 21:00 or later. Embrace the late Greek dining culture — it's part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rent bicycles and cycle along a coastal road or trail to a nearby village or viewpoint. The morning is the best time before the heat peaks. Stop for photos and take in panoramic sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon — this time try a different section of the resort beach or a nearby public beach. Bring a good book and simply enjoy the warm sea and sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beach bar, followed by dinner at a mezze restaurant where you can order many small dishes to share.

meals.breakfast: Café in the village reached by bicycle — fresh orange juice, a cheese-and-tomato toasted sandwich, and Greek coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack — fresh fruit, a cold sesame breadstick (koulouri), and sparkling water from a kiosk (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Mezze restaurant — 6–8 shared small plates including saganaki, grilled vegetables, meatballs (keftedes), and taramasalata with wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rentals typically cost €8–15/day. Start the ride before 9:00 AM to avoid peak heat. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local monastery or hilltop chapel for panoramic views and a moment of cultural reflection. These are usually free to enter and offer stunning vistas over the sea and coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort — use the pool, enjoy a light spa treatment if available (a massage or facial for €40–70), and pack/reorganize your bag as the trip winds down.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a new restaurant you haven't tried yet — ask locals or resort staff for their personal recommendation rather than a tourist guide pick.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs, fresh tomatoes, olives, feta, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a hilltop café near the monastery — spanakopita, a cold drink, and fresh fruit (€9–13)
meals.dinner: Locally recommended restaurant — whatever is the specialty of the house. Budget €22–30 per person. Try to order something you haven't had yet on the trip.

day_by_day.notes: When visiting monasteries or churches, dress modestly — shoulders and knees should be covered. Many provide wraps at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — make the most of the warm Aegean. Swim, float, and absorb the atmosphere. Collect a small handful of smooth sea pebbles as a free, natural memento.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the local village — pick up local honey, olive oil, dried herbs, or handmade ceramics. These make excellent gifts and are reasonably priced at local shops versus tourist traps.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — return to your favorite restaurant from the trip or try the most special place you've been saving. Toast the journey with a bottle of local wine.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — treat yourself to everything on offer
meals.lunch: Casual beach snack — fresh watermelon, a cold beer, and a gyros wrap (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite spot — 3-course meal: starter, grilled fish or meat main, and a dessert of baklava or galaktoboureko with Greek brandy (metaxa) (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight so the final morning is stress-free. Keep a small bag ready with essentials for the last morning before checkout.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last swim or sunrise walk on the beach. Check out of the resort. Depending on your flight time, store luggage at the hotel and enjoy a final coffee at a beachside café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to the airport. Allow plenty of time for travel, check-in, and security. Browse duty-free for any last Greek products (mastiha gum, Greek coffee, or local spirits).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the memories of 13 days of sun, sea, and incredible food back home.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a local café — yogurt with honey, a bougatsa pastry, and a double freddo espresso (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Airport meal or a final quick bite near the resort before transfer — keep it light for travel
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the destination airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight details, transfer timing, and checkout time with the resort the night before. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport procedures in Greek airports during peak summer season.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to get your bearings and soak in the first views of the Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort's infinity pool as the sun begins to lower. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the beachside bar before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Light mezze and fresh juice at the resort's beach café upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant – fresh catch of the day, grilled octopus, and local Assyrtiko white wine

day_by_day.notes: Request an early check-in when booking if possible. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. The resort concierge can assist with booking all upcoming experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a lavish buffet breakfast at the resort overlooking the sea. Afterward, spend the morning on the resort's private beach – swim in the warm Aegean, try paddleboarding or kayaking offered by the resort's water sports center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion along the nearby coastline. Explore hidden sea caves, anchor at a secluded cove for snorkeling, and enjoy the crystal-clear turquoise water. The boat crew can prepare fresh fruit and chilled beverages on board.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa treatment – opt for a traditional Greek olive oil massage or a sea salt scrub. Dine at a nearby acclaimed seafood taverna with harbor views.

meals.breakfast: Luxury buffet at the resort – pastries, fresh fruit, eggs to order, smoked salmon, Greek yogurt with thyme honey
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket on the private boat – artisan cheeses, cured meats, olives, pita, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Premium seafood taverna: grilled whole sea bass, prawn saganaki, hand-cut fries, and a bottle of local Moschofilero

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat excursion through the resort concierge at least one day in advance. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga session on the beach offered by the resort (optional). Follow with a Greek-style breakfast. Head out for a guided walking tour of the nearest traditional village – explore whitewashed alleys, Byzantine churches, and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive oil estate or winery for a private tasting experience. Learn about the production of extra-virgin olive oil or indigenous Greek grape varieties, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner on your terrace or balcony, arranged by the resort with a curated menu and a sommelier-selected wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Greek breakfast at the resort – spanakopita, tiropita, Kalamata olives, fresh tomatoes, feta, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Tasting menu at the olive oil estate or winery – seasonal produce, local cheeses, house-cured meats, and wine pairings
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or terrace dinner curated by the resort chef – lamb chops with herb jus, roasted vegetables, and baklava for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private estate visit and in-suite dinner with the concierge the evening before. Dress code for the estate is smart casual.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private guided tour of a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic ruins. A knowledgeable local historian will provide an immersive narrative of ancient Greek civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a premium beach club in the area for the afternoon. Enjoy a VIP sunbed reservation, refreshing cocktails, and a dip in the sea. The beach club setting offers stunning views and a vibrant yet relaxed atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local marina or harbor area on foot. Browse boutique shops and galleries before settling in for dinner at a top-rated restaurant known for its modern Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort – avocado toast with feta, poached eggs, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a Greek frappe
meals.lunch: Gourmet beach club menu – lobster linguine, grilled calamari, watermelon and feta salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Modern Greek fine dining: beef tenderloin with truffle-infused skordalia, sea urchin pasta, and a premium Greek red wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Reserve VIP sunbeds at the beach club in advance as they fill quickly during peak season. Bring cash for tips at local establishments.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at the resort pool. Enjoy a poolside breakfast and then book a private paddleboard or stand-up kayak session along the calm morning waters of the cove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with a local chef – learn to prepare traditional Greek dishes such as moussaka, tzatziki, dolmades, and loukoumades. The class takes place in a scenic local kitchen or outdoor setting.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class at a communal table, paired with local wines. Return to the resort for a nightcap at the rooftop or terrace bar, taking in the star-lit Aegean sky.

meals.breakfast: Poolside breakfast at the resort – fresh fruit platter, granola with Greek yogurt, honey, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class served as a full meal with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort bar – mezze platter, bruschetta, and a glass of chilled white wine or cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is typically 3–4 hours. Wear comfortable clothes. This is one of the most memorable cultural experiences of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private yacht charter begins. Depart from the local marina after a resort breakfast. Sail to a nearby uninhabited island or secluded bay accessible only by boat. Snorkel, swim, and sunbathe on pristine shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue sailing to a second scenic stop – perhaps a sea cave or a famous blue lagoon. The yacht crew will prepare a gourmet lunch on board with fresh local ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Sail back along the coast at golden hour for spectacular views. Return to the resort, freshen up, and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a renowned local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: On-board gourmet lunch prepared by the yacht chef – grilled prawns, Greek salad, stuffed peppers, fresh bread, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant: slow-roasted lamb with orzo, grilled halloumi, village salad, and a carafe of house red wine

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private yacht charters should be booked well in advance. Bring sunscreen, a hat, a light cover-up, and motion sickness tablets if needed. Tip the crew generously.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in, enjoy a late breakfast at the resort, and spend the morning reading on the beach or having a spa session. Opt for a couple's treatment or a traditional hammam experience at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby local market or artisan fair. Sample street food, browse handmade ceramics, jewelry, and local produce. Pick up premium souvenirs such as saffron, mastiha products, or handwoven textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise on a smaller vessel or catamaran – sip champagne while watching the sun dip into the Aegean. Return to the resort for a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at the resort – eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and a Bloody Mary or mimosa
meals.lunch: Street food at the local market – souvlaki, spanakopita, loukoumades with honey, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Champagne and canapés on the sunset cruise, followed by a light mezze dinner back at the resort bar

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to slow down and recharge mid-trip. The local market is best visited in the morning or early afternoon before vendors begin to pack up.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a guided jeep or 4x4 off-road tour of the island's or region's interior. Visit panoramic viewpoints, hidden monasteries, and traditional mountain villages inaccessible by regular vehicles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a traditional taverna in a hilltop village for a long, leisurely lunch. Explore the village on foot afterward – admire the architecture, chat with locals, and visit a small family-run shop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a sunset swim in the sea before a sophisticated dinner at a restaurant specializing in Cretan or regional Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the resort – village bread, local honey, fresh tomatoes, feta, cured meats, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional village taverna: slow-cooked goat stew, roasted potatoes, horta (wild greens), and house wine from the barrel
meals.dinner: Regional fine-dining restaurant: dakos salad, stuffed zucchini blossoms, slow-braised pork with honey and thyme, and local dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the village exploration. Bring a light layer as mountain areas can be slightly cooler than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on the beach. Try a new water sport – jet skiing, parasailing, or windsurfing offered by the resort or a nearby operator. Enjoy the warm sea and clear skies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private food tour of the local town or village. A culinary guide will take you through the best local producers, bakeries, cheese shops, and specialty food stores, with tastings at each stop.
day_by_day.evening: Reserve a table at one of the area's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants for a special multi-course tasting menu with wine pairings. This is the showstopper dinner of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort – yogurt parfait, seasonal fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Generous tastings throughout the food tour serve as lunch – cheeses, cured meats, pastries, local wines, and artisan products
meals.dinner: Flagship fine-dining experience: 7-course tasting menu featuring the best of Greek seasonal produce, paired with premium Greek wines selected by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Book the fine-dining dinner reservation at least one week in advance as top restaurants fill quickly in June. Smart casual or semi-formal attire is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a peaceful morning at the resort. Take a guided snorkeling tour along a nearby reef or underwater landscape with a marine guide who can identify local sea life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby historical site, museum, or Byzantine castle. Hire a private guide for a personalized and in-depth experience. Browse the gift shop for quality reproductions or art books.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a cliffside or hilltop restaurant with panoramic sea views. Enjoy a leisurely dinner as the lights of the coast twinkle below.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – smoked salmon bagel, poached eggs, fresh juice, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the historical site – club sandwich, fresh salad, and iced tea
meals.dinner: Cliffside restaurant: grilled lobster, saffron risotto, roasted beet salad, and a bottle of premium Greek white wine

day_by_day.notes: Carry water and sun protection for the afternoon historical site visit. Evening at the cliffside restaurant is best enjoyed at sunset – ask for a window or terrace table.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day beach hopping by private speedboat. Visit three or four of the most beautiful beaches in the region, each with its own character – some with dramatic cliffs, others with soft white sand and shallow turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at the most scenic beach for an extended swim and relaxation. The boat captain will recommend the best spots based on conditions. Enjoy a packed gourmet lunch on board.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a cocktail hour at the resort bar. Dinner at a renowned local restaurant with a focus on wood-fired and charcoal-grilled meats and seafood.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the speedboat – artisan bread, hummus, grilled vegetables, cold cuts, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water and wine
meals.dinner: Charcoal grill restaurant: whole grilled sea bream, lamb chops, grilled vegetables, tzatziki, and a robust Greek red wine

day_by_day.notes: Beach hopping by speedboat is weather-dependent. The resort concierge can advise on the best beaches based on wind conditions that day.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning at the beach. Swim, relax, and take in the beauty of the Aegean one last time. Opt for a farewell spa treatment or a relaxing facial at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the local town. Visit a high-end boutique for handcrafted gold jewelry, quality leather sandals, or premium olive oil and mastiha products to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant or a special pre-booked private beach dinner. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a bottle of premium Greek Champagne-method sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the resort – full spread with all favorites from the trip
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local café or beach bar – grilled fish, Greek salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner arranged by the resort: candlelit table in the sand, bespoke menu by the chef, and a sommelier-curated wine experience

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private beach dinner at least two days in advance. Pack any fragile souvenirs carefully. Confirm checkout time and arrange airport transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a last walk along the beach, breathe in the sea air, and capture any final photos. Check out of the resort and ensure all luggage is prepared.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Depart Greece with extraordinary memories of beaches, food, culture, and the warm Aegean sun.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – enjoy every last bite of Greek yogurt, thyme honey, fresh pastries, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport lounge or a quick bite at a café near the terminal
meals.dinner: On the plane or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport procedures. The resort concierge can arrange a premium airport transfer with a professional driver. Consider joining a Greek wine club or ordering specialty products online to relive the flavors at home.
